title: InvarOS Qualification Transcript v1
description: What a shipped subject build observed when exercised against named criteria. Carries no verdict: the schema defines no status field and closes every object, so a subject cannot emit a signed verdict inside this artifact. See invaros/ADR-002 and founder decision QE-D2.

declaredAbsence.description: A stated absence, drawn from a closed vocabulary. ONE self-describing value carrying both the fact of absence and its cause, so a sentinel and its reason cannot drift apart -- there is only one field to get wrong. Extending this set is a schema change, which is the correct friction. Cannot collide with a digest: the prefixes differ.

digestOrDeclaredAbsence.description: Either a real digest of real bytes, or an explicit stated absence. NEVER a digest of something else. Substituting a neighbouring digest for a missing one makes an absent input indistinguishable from a present one in a signed artifact -- the defect recorded as QE1-F1 during Phase 1 execution, which this form exists to make unrepresentable.

criteria.description: Exactly one criteria set, per QE-D12. This member is an object and is never an array; composition across criteria kinds belongs to consumers, not to this schema. The digest pins the whole criteria set for a profile, per QE-D11.

kind.description: Only conformance-vectors is in Phase 1 scope. The remaining values are defined so that adding a criteria kind later is not a schema change.

manifest_digest.description: NORMATIVE: computed from the criteria bytes the harness actually consumed, never from a declared or configured value (QE-D13). Not expressible in schema; enforced by test V14 in the producing repository.

specification_digest.description: NORMATIVE: the digest of the specification bytes the harness actually read, or a declared absence. It is NEVER any other digest. A producer that cannot resolve the specification states so; it does not substitute. Enforced by the producing repository's emission tests, and by the verifier, which reports a specification digest equal to the criteria manifest digest as a finding.

coverage.description: Absence is stated, never inferred (architecture P5). units_not_executed is required, so omitting a gap is not expressible.

reasonCode.description: Closed vocabulary, per QE-D7. The distinction between a subject capability gap (not-implemented) and a qualification-apparatus coverage gap (environment-unavailable) must be available to automated consumers without parsing free text; detail is advisory only. In this artifact the reason code is the subject's factual report of what it did not execute. In an attestation it is verifier-derived, and a disagreement between the two is a reportable finding.

observation.description: What the subject observed. There is deliberately no expected value here: expected_echo was removed by QE-D13, and criteria.manifest_digest serves its purpose. Recording an expectation would give the transcript a self-scoring surface.

architecture.description: Closed vocabulary of execution architectures. Closed deliberately: the matched-pair constraint on the environment object is expressible only over a finite set, and an open string would make cross-architecture qualification representable again. Adding an architecture is a schema change, which is the correct friction (QE-D17).

environment.description:
Where the observations were produced. Under founder decision QE-D17 the subject is qualified in its own native architecture and execution environment; a development-host substitute is not equivalent.

V21 -- INVARIANT. A transcript that names a subject architecture differing from its host architecture is not merely invalid, it is INEXPRESSIBLE: there is ONE architecture member, which is simultaneously the subject's and the host's. Two members constrained to be equal would permit an invalid state and then forbid it, and would give a producer two fields to get wrong; one member cannot drift from itself. This is the same reasoning declaredAbsence above states for carrying a fact and its cause in a single value.

The producer still derives the two independently -- the subject's ELF machine type from the subject bytes, the host's from uname -- and REFUSES TO EMIT when they disagree, so the check is real rather than assumed. That refusal is a normative requirement no schema can express, enforced by a negative-control test in the producing repository, exactly as criteria.manifest_digest is.

The identity members are OPTIONAL rather than required, deliberately. Requiring them would invalidate transcripts that were valid when emitted, which §9.1 forbids without a v2 and which would retroactively redefine Phase 1 against DECISION_20260806_ENVIRONMENT_EQUIVALENT_QUALIFICATION.md §5.1. This amendment is therefore strictly narrowing: nothing valid before is invalid now. Omission is caught where it is detectable -- the producer always emits them, and the verifier reports environment-identity-absent as a finding. That is the QE1-F1 pattern: remove the motive in the schema, detect the act in the verifier.

architecture.description: The one execution architecture of both the subject and the host. See the V21 note above for why this is a single member.

environment_id.description:
Names the execution environment class the transcript is bound to -- for example openwrt-aarch64 or linux-x86_64. It identifies an environment CLASS, never a device: no device or platform is uniquely canonical (QE-D17), and a per-device identifier here would introduce deployment identity into the vendor evidence population, which QE-D21 keeps out of it.

The pattern requires the class to END in one of the architectures of the closed vocabulary above, so that the self-asserted half of this member cannot name an architecture the schema does not know. The schema cannot check that the suffix equals the sibling architecture member -- JSON Schema compares no two members -- so the producer checks that, against the architecture it derived from the subject's ELF header, and refuses to emit on disagreement.

signature.description: ES256, reusing the Runtime's existing signing substrate per founder decision QE-D15. Byte profile: P-256, SHA-256, 64-octet fixed-width r||s, unpadded base64url, key id = SHA-256 over DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo. ed25519 is not permitted in v1.
